rationale: Both validate the characters, extract the digits and apply the area and exchange checks in the same way. B's length validation maps directly onto the error messages: fewer than 10, more than 11, then 11 digits not starting with 1, before the country code is stripped. A strips the leading 1 first and then raises 'must not be greater than 11 digits' when the length is greater than 10, so the reader has to work out why the condition and the message disagree. B names the cleaned value digits instead of rebinding the parameter, and pretty() reuses the area_code property. B's allowed-punctuation string contains a harmless duplicated '()', which is sloppy, but the overall control flow is clearer and easier to verify.
